questions.q: What are the three choices Goewey says you always have when facing a stressful situation?
a: Change it, leave it, or accept it
Ignore it, fight it, or surrender to it
Analyze it, plan it, or act on it
Deny it, delay it, or delegate it
questions.why: From the lesson on changing, leaving, or accepting stressful situations.

questions.q: What example does the text give for a stressful situation?
a: Losing your job because an executive committed tax fraud
Getting fired for consistently poor performance
Being passed over for a promotion you expected
Having your company go bankrupt overnight
questions.why: From the lesson on changing, leaving, or accepting, using the job loss example.

questions.q: What two exercises does Goewey suggest for developing a peaceful mindset?
a: Start your day with peace and quiet, and take a 30-second time-out a couple times a day
Meditate for an hour each morning and journal at night
Practice deep breathing before bed and walk outside daily
Write down three gratitudes and do a body scan each evening
questions.why: From the lesson on practicing a peaceful mindset every day.

questions.q: What did Henry Beecher do during World War II when he ran out of morphine?
a: He infused soldiers with saline solution while telling them they were getting morphine
He gave them a lower dose of a different painkiller
He used a combination of herbal remedies instead
He told them to focus on positive memories to cope
questions.why: From the lesson on the placebo effect, describing Beecher's WWII experience.

questions.q: What percentage of soldiers reported immense pain relief from the saline solution?
questions.why: From the lesson on the placebo effect, citing the 40% figure.
